errors.description: The model hallucinated a second orange line that does not exist in the video. The Scene Description explicitly states only 6 ropes were generated, each with a unique color (yellow, orange, green, blue, red, white). The model incorrectly interpreted overlapping segments or visual artifacts as a separate seventh line, likely due to misperceiving the spatial structure or motion of the ropes during drawing.

analysis_result.analysis: The model correctly identified the task as counting distinct lines and enumerated visible lines in the final frame. However, it hallucinated a seventh line — a second orange rope — which was not present in the video. This error stems from misinterpreting visual complexity (e.g., overlapping curves or motion trails) as an additional distinct object. The model’s reasoning was otherwise logically consistent: it counted each perceived line once. The failure is perceptual (misseeing a non-existent object), not logical — the counting method itself was sound given its misperception. This is a major error because it directly led to an incorrect final answer (7 instead of 6).
